question:
A hydrogen-like ion (single-electron system) has nuclear charge $+Ze$ and Bohr energy levels given by $E_n=-13.6\,\text{eV}\,\dfrac{Z^2}{n^2}$, where $n$ is the principal quantum number.

It undergoes an emission transition from $n=2$ to $n=1$.

You are also given that the ionisation energy of a hydrogen atom from its ground state ($n=1$) is $13.6\,\text{eV}$.

Design and evaluate the condition on the atomic number $Z$ such that the photon emitted in the $2\to 1$ transition of the hydrogen-like ion has enough energy to ionise a ground-state hydrogen atom. Clearly justify the condition and state the smallest possible integer value of $Z$ that satisfies it.
